question.leadin: During the Japanese invasion, this man led resistance forces from a base on the sacred Paektu Mountain.
question.text: Name this first North Korean leader who invaded South Korea to begin the Korean War.
question.answerHtml: Kim Il-sung [prompt on “Kim”; do not accept or prompt on “Il-sung”]
question.clue: This man's government was involved in conflict with the U.S. in the Axe Murder Incident and the capture of the Pueblo.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian political families.
swap.text: One member of this family led South Korea between 1961 and 1979. His daughter was impeached as president due to influence peddling by Choi Soon-sil.
swap.clue: One of these in London contains the Speakers' Corner, adjoins Kensington Gardens, and was the site of the Crystal Palace.

question.leadin: Name some things about historically significant Summer Olympics.
question.text: The June Democracy Movement occurred before the 1988 Olympics in this city, leading to the establishment of the Sixth Republic in its nation in an effort to prevent the establishment of a military junta before the Olympics.
question.clue: The Han River runs through this city, and it shares an administrative region with Gyeonggi Province and Incheon.

swap.leadin: The yangban served as this dynasty's bureaucracy after passing the gwageo exam.
swap.text: Sejong the Great was a member of what Korean dynasty which was opposed by the Donghak Uprising?
swap.clue: This final dynastic kingdom of Korea that lasted from 1392 to 1897 when it was replaced by the Korean Empire. Sejong the Great established the Hall of Worthies in this kingdom.

question.text: Throughout the 16th century, naval vessels called "turtle ships" repeatedly repelled Japanese invasions of this final Korean dynasty that lasted from 1392 until the early 20th century.
question.clue: This hermit dynasty of Korea which succeeded the Goryeo and ran from approximately 1392 to 1897.

swap.leadin: This man ordered "do not announce my death" after he was fatally shot at Noryang.
swap.text: Name this 16th-century admiral who orchestrated huge victories such as Myeongnyang [mee-yong-n'yong] for Korea during the Imjin War against Japan.

question.leadin: This kingdom ultimately broke up into the a group known as the Three Kingdoms, which included Baekje and Goguryeo.
question.text: This kingdom was ruled by the Gyeongju Kim clan for nearly 1000 years, making it one of the longest-surviving dynasties in history. Its aristocrats were called "sacred bone" or "true bone".
question.clue: Confucianism in Korea built upon earlier hierarchies such as the bone-rank system, which was used by this kingdom. This kingdom unified Korea in the 7th century after defeating its rivals Baekje and Goguryeo.

swap.text: During the Korean War, Douglas MacArthur planned and executed this naval landing, allowing UN forces to break out of the Pusan perimeter.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Inch (e)on [accept Incheon Sangnyuk Jakjeon; accept Operation Chromite]

question.text: During the war, the northwest of North Korea gained this nickname from UN forces, due to the presence of Soviet fighter planes here. Along the Yalu River, this region was the site of many dogfights.
question.clue: During the war, U.N. pilots also referred to the northwest of Korea as "[these planes] Alley," since Americans F-86 Sabres often encountered Soviet aircraft there.

swap.leadin: Time to see how much you know about East Asian naval battles.
swap.text: In this last stand of the Korean navy, Admiral Yi Sun-Sin defeated a Japanese fleet of over 10 times his size with only 13 ships, destroying half the Japanese fleet. It is widely regarded as his greatest victory.
swap.clue: Joseon was invaded twice by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's forces in the Imjin War but were driven back at this 1597 naval engagement by Admiral Yi Sun-sin despite the Japanese outnumbering the Korean fleet at least 10 to 1.

question.text: This kingdom emerged victorious from the Three Kingdoms Period in 668, and then kicked out their allies, the Tang Dynasty, soon after.
question.clue: This kingdom included the hereditary "head rank 6" caste in its "bone rank" system, and used highly-educated elite knights whose name means "flower boys."

swap.leadin: Name these Asian politicians who had European wives.
swap.text: This first president of South Korea assumed dictatorial powers when the Korean War broke out, and was exiled with his Austrian wife Franziska Donner to Hawaii after his overthrow in a 1960 coup.
swap.clue: This ruler, who put down the Jeju uprising at the beginning of his rule, was forced into exile in Hawaii by the 1960 April Revolution, and he was replaced by Yun Bosun.

question.leadin: An empress from this dynasty was assassinated on the orders of Miura Goro, after which men were ordered to cut off the top knot of their hair.
question.text: Name this dynasty that succeeded the Goryeo, whose kings included Sejong the Great. This was the last dynastic kingdom of Korea.
question.clue: As he died, a military leader of this kingdom instructed, "Beat my war drums. Do not announce my death."

swap.leadin: In 1866, France occupied this island for six weeks following the execution of seven Catholic missionaries during a crackdown on Christians initiated by Heungseon Daewongun.
swap.text: Name this island, where the Japanese ship Un'yo provoked a battle that led to an 1876 unequal treaty named for it. That treaty named for this island ended the Joseon Kingdom's status as a tributary of the Qing Dynasty.

question.leadin: This dynasty commissioned a version of The Prescribed Ritual Text of the Past and Present that became the first book printed in moveable type.
question.text: Name this dynasty whose founder constructed ten Buddhist monasteries and popularized the Jogye Order which had been founded during an earlier dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Goryeo dynasty [accept Koryo; do not accept or prompt on Goguryeo or Korea alone]
question.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").

swap.text: Following Park's assassination, Chun Doo-hwan declared martial law, leading to this series of student uprisings at Chonnam University. Jurgen Hinzpeter was the only one to capture these protests on film.
swap.clue: The date of this event and the area code where it occurred are referenced in the lyric "everyone dial it, 062-518."

question.leadin: Identify the following about Korean history FTPE.
question.text: This first native Korean state arose near the Yalu River in the first century CE and conquered the Chinese colony of Lolang.
question.clue: Under Yang, China attempted to conquer this kingdom, which opposed Baekje and Silla during the Korean Three Kingdoms Period. That invasion failed after the Battle of the Salsu River.

swap.text: In 935, General Wang Kon overthrew the Silla Kingdom to establish this successor state, which ruled the peninsula until 1392 and produced valuable celadon ceramics.

question.leadin: This ruler worked with missionary Horace G. Underwood and nurse Annie Ellers to establish separate prestigious academies for boys and girls.
question.text: Name this wife of King Gojong and victim to the Eulmi Incident who allotted a separate "American farm," reorganized the bureaucracy, sent her relative on the "American Expedition" and dealt with fallout from an 1882 insurrection.

swap.leadin: Name the following Christianity-inspired rebellions in Asia, FTPE.
swap.text: This Korean uprising shares its name with a religious movement that contained Christian elements despite its founder Choe Che-u's distaste of Western influence. Simultaneous Japanese and Chinese attempts to quell the rebellion led to the First Sino-Japanese War.
